items.label: Table 1, CITATION_PLUS_MESH: 5x2 CV on 1987-2010, held-out 2011 and 2012

assumptions.what: The paper's 'human-related' PubMed query is in its lost supplement. We use humans[mh] AND hasabstract AND english[la], 1987-2012, from the PubMed 2026 baseline
assumptions.sensitivity: Chosen by RCT_PT count among four candidate queries (E-utilities, 2026-11-19): humans[mh] alone gives 312,580 RCT_PT citations, with hasabstract 301,496, with hasabstract and english[la] 284,086, against the paper's 277,789. Our dataset holds 6,164,168 citations, 278,869 with RCT_PT, and 5,310,239 in 1987-2010 (the paper: 'over 5 million').

assumptions.what: MEDLINE records as of the 2026 baseline, not the 2012-2014 download; old baselines are not distributed
assumptions.sensitivity: NLM corrects publication types and MeSH over time. The RCT_PT count of our dataset is within 278,869 of 277,789 (0.4%), so the drift in the label is small in total; which citations changed cannot be known.

assumptions.what: Publication year: the PubDate year, or the first year of MedlineDate
assumptions.sensitivity: PubMed's [dp] also matches electronic dates; the year split moves a few citations between training and test years.

assumptions.what: The 7.5% training sample is drawn with NumPy seed 0; the paper gives no seed
assumptions.sensitivity: 398,268 citations, 17,919 with RCT_PT. A different sample moves the test measures by about the cross-validation spread (see the variants).

assumptions.what: Feature sets: title and abstract uni-, bi- and trigrams, journal, author names, author count, author keywords (citation); MeSH descriptors, major descriptors, descriptor/qualifier pairs and substances (MeSH). The paper's list is in the supplement
assumptions.sensitivity: The paper names the kinds (title n-grams 1-3, bibliographic fields, MeSH) but not the list. Our candidates hold 54 million features in the training sample against the paper's 'approximately 45 million'.

assumptions.what: Tokens split on whitespace and punctuation, lower case, the SMART stop words of McCallum's Bag-Of-Words library, no stemming
assumptions.sensitivity: From the same group's description of the same pipeline in 2018 (Cohen et al., PMC6146117), not from this paper.

assumptions.what: Structured-abstract labels (BACKGROUND:, METHODS:) kept in the abstract text
assumptions.sensitivity: Not tested; labels are a handful of tokens per abstract.

assumptions.what: LIBLINEAR -s 1 (L2-regularized L2-loss SVM, dual), C = 1, with a bias term (-B 1), binary features without row scaling
assumptions.sensitivity: LIBLINEAR's defaults; the paper states none of them. variants.json: C = 0.1, unit-length rows and logistic regression each move the 2011 measures; see the cause.

assumptions.what: Forward selection with one 2-fold split per candidate instead of 5x2 CV; a set is added when it raises AUC at four decimals, F1 breaking ties
assumptions.sensitivity: 5x2 CV at every step would take about 6 hours here; the final models are cross-validated 5x2 as in the paper. The paper does not say how AUC and F1 are combined; the rule follows the group's 2018 paper.

assumptions.what: Confidence: Platt's sigmoid fitted to 2-fold out-of-fold margins of the training sample, in place of the paper's 'extension to the method of Ruping', which is described only in the supplement
assumptions.sensitivity: Changes only the MSE rows. The zero-centred sigmoid baseline is the paper's own definition.

cause.summary: Rebuilt from the paper's text on the 2026 MEDLINE baseline: the feature-set list, the LIBLINEAR settings, the selection rule, the confidence method and the PubMed query are in the lost supplement, and NLM has corrected records since 2012-2014. Every AUC, average precision, F1 and accuracy is within 0.008 of the printed value (the largest gap: CITATION_ONLY F1 on 2012, 0.803 against 0.811), and our calibrated MSE within 0.001. The zero-centred sigmoid MSE is 0.007 to 0.009 higher than printed: it depends on the scale of the SVM margin, which the unstated C and feature scaling set.

hypotheses.test: Count RCT_PT citations in our dataset against the paper's 277,789 (dataset.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: An unstated LIBLINEAR setting (C, row scaling, loss) moves the measures onto the paper's
hypotheses.test: Retrain the forward-selection models with C = 0.1 and unit-length rows, one at a time, and evaluate on 2011 (variants.json). cause.summary: As for Tables 1 and 2, and the CHISQ test is not described: at p < 0.05 our filter keeps 2,628,721 and 2,651,049 features against the paper's 102,023 and 113,177, so our CHISQ models are larger and score as high as the paper's or higher, and our POSTHOC models, cut to the same count, are close to forward selection by construction. Our forward-selection models keep 53,810,398 and 54,035,744 features against 44,114,421 and 34,636,788, because selection kept more sets (abstract trigrams alone hold 35 million).

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper's CHISQ threshold was much stricter than p < 0.05
hypotheses.test: Count the features each threshold keeps and refit CHISQ and POSTHOC at the Bonferroni threshold (variants.json). CITATION_ONLY kept: p < 0.05: 2,628,721, p < 0.001: 191,826, p < 1e-6: 71,853, Bonferroni: 46,126; refitted CHISQ AUC 0.926, AP 0.745, F1 0.713, POSTHOC AUC 0.951, AP 0.814, F1 0.775. CITATION_PLUS_MESH kept: p < 0.05: 2,651,049, p < 0.001: 203,591, p < 1e-6: 79,034, Bonferroni: 51,194; CHISQ AUC 0.941, AP 0.780, F1 0.742, POSTHOC AUC 0.961, AP 0.844, F1 0.799. The paper's CHISQ feature counts and CHISQ scores lie between our p < 0.05 and Bonferroni models (MeSH CHISQ F1 equals our p < 0.05 model's at printed precision), so its threshold lay between them; the POSTHOC scores do not bracket; no threshold was fitted to the paper
